surprises.description: Hanmi’s diluted EPS was $0.80, below both the preview’s $0.808 consensus estimate and its $0.82 base case. The gap was small, but the headline result came in slightly below expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net income rose to $23.7 million, or $0.80 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS **$0.808**”; the preview’s base case showed “Diluted EPS **$0.82**.”

surprises.description: NIM reached 3.44%, above the preview’s 3.40% base case and its 3.40% “good” threshold. However, roughly half of the 8-basis-point sequential expansion came from non-recurring items, limiting the recurring improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded 8 basis points to 3.44%, though roughly 4 basis points (about $700,000) came from non-recurring items like loan prepayment fees and a special FHLB dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NIM 3.40%” in the base case; the checklist says “≥3.40% validates the refi math and the asset-sensitivity case.”

surprises.description: The reported annual interest-expense saving from the subordinated-debt refinancing was far below the preview’s estimate: $550,000 annually rather than about $4.1 million. That is a substantial shortfall against a benefit the preview expected management to confirm and quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hanmi refinanced subordinated debt (issuing $55 million of 2036 notes to redeem $110 million of 2031 notes), cutting annual interest expense by $550,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$4.1M annualized” savings from replacing the $110 million notes and said to confirm the redemption and “get the Q4 run-rate benefit (~$1.0M/qtr pretax).”

surprises.description: Credit expense rose to $4.5 million, well above the preview’s $1.8 million base case, as a previously identified CRE loan generated a $3.2 million partial charge-off. The preview discussed this size of provision only in its bear scenario; the expected clean-credit/base case did not anticipate this charge-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Credit loss expense jumped to $4.5 million from $1.2 million, driven by a $3.2 million partial charge-off on a previously identified CRE loan now being sold in Q4, pushing annualized net charge-offs to 27 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case projected “provision $1.8M” and described credit as “isolated,” with “no new classifieds”; the bear case projected “provision $4.5M+.”

surprises.description: Loan production surged, but unusually high payoffs prevented balance growth, and management’s 2026 outlook stepped down from the preview’s low-to-mid-single-digit expectation to low-single-digit growth. The reported increase in payoffs—including borrowers refinancing elsewhere for looser terms—makes the growth outlook weaker than the preview’s hoped-for H2 acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loan production surged 46.2% sequentially to $544 million … but payoffs of $283 million kept net loan balances roughly flat”; year-to-date payoffs “increased 65% versus last year,” with “over one-third driven by borrowers refinancing to other lenders offering looser terms.” Management guided to “low-single-digit loan growth for full-year 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide was “low-to-mid single digits” and that it “requires H2 acceleration”; its base case expected management to “reaffirm low-to-mid single-digit loan growth.”

surprises.description: Corporate Korea deposits exceeded the preview’s already-record $1.2 billion level, rising to over $1.3 billion and 19% of total deposits. But USKC loans fell 5%, so the deposit growth was not accompanied by the utilization or lending inflection the preview identified as a possible upside development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corporate Korea (USKC) deposits grew 12% to over $1.3 billion, reaching a record 19% of total deposits, while USKC loans fell 5% to $780 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$1.2B of deposits (17% of total)” and said “any sign of line utilization inflecting is a 2027 earnings unlock.”

surprises.description: Unrealized losses on available-for-sale securities increased by $16.5 million after tax, an adverse balance-sheet development not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the rate environment or earnings risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unrealized AFS securities losses rose $16.5 million after-tax.”
